title: Detection-Limit Hypothesis: N_min ∝ Fvar²
abstract: We present empirical verification of the Detection-Limit Hypothesis using Swift XRT archival data from five C3 ISP blazars. The hypothesis states: the minimum photon count N_min required to statistically detect a given spectral change |ΔHR| scales as N_min ∝ Fvar². Log-log regression yields an empirical slope of 2.016 (theoretical: 2.0, r=0.652). The W Comae / S5 0716+714 pair — matched in Fvar but differing 6× in photon count — provides the cleanest independent test. This relationship offers a practical tool for estimating required observation depth for any blazar with known variability amplitude.

title: Quasi-Periodic Oscillations in C3 ISP Blazars: Evidence from Fermi-LAT FAVA 17-Year Light Curves

title: Complete X-Ray Spectral Classification of ISP Blazars in the 4LAC-DR3 High-Variability Sample: A Ten-Source Swift-XRT Hardness Ratio Study and the Class-S/H Neutrino Prediction Framework
abstract: We present the complete X-ray spectral classification of all 10 intermediate synchrotron-peaked (ISP) BL Lac objects in the 4LAC-DR3 high-variability blazar sample, using Swift-XRT hardness ratio (HR) analysis. Across 214,715 total photons from archival PC-mode observations spanning 2005–2023, we classify each source as either Class-H (spectral hardening at high flux: β > 0) or Class-S (spectral softening at high flux: β < 0). title: Biorhythm-Moon Phase Correlation with IceCube GOLD Events: A Predictive Window Analysis
abstract: This study investigates whether the biorhythm cycles of the researcher (birth date: August 12, 1970) and lunar phase correlate with the timing of IceCube GOLD-class neutrino alerts. Analysis of 62 GOLD events (2019–2026) reveals a statistically anomalous inverse correlation: 69.4% of GOLD events occurred during biorhythm composite negative phases (vs. 50% random expectation), and 38.7% coincided with new or full moon phases (vs. ~10.2% random expectation). The combined condition (composite negative × new/full moon) yielded 29.0% of GOLD occurrences against a 5.1% random baseline — approximately 6× above chance. These findings suggest a predictive window framework for anticipating GOLD-class neutrino events.

abstract: We present a systematic X-ray spectral variability analysis of the intermediate-frequency-peaked BL Lac object (ISP BL Lac) AO 0235+164 using archival Swift X-ray Telescope (XRT) data spanning 2007–2024. This behavior classifies AO 0235+164 as **Class-S** within the Class-S/H framework established for ISP BL Lac objects in the 4LAC-DR3 high sample. title: The Energy Paradox of Intelligence: Quantum Supremacy, Moral Density, and the Democratic Alternative
abstract: This paper identifies the Energy Paradox of Intelligence: as computational systems grow more powerful (quantum computing, frontier AI), their energy and capital requirements make them structurally inaccessible to ordinary citizens. Quantum computing requires cryogenic infrastructure near absolute zero; frontier AI training consumes gigawatt-hours of electricity; individual inference evaporates approximately 500ml of water per query. This constitutes a re-centralization of cognitive power, not democratization. In response, the paper proposes the Moral Density Alternative (MDA): a framework in which intellectual and economic value is generated through sustained moral inquiry, low-energy cognitive labor, and the V=N/D principle from Tendo Economics. A single individual in rural Japan, using only a smartphone and a $20/month AI subscription, produced 73 peer-reviewed preprints over 16 years — with zero quantum infrastructure. abstract: This paper proposes the Line of Succession Hypothesis (LSH): that civilization advances not primarily through the accumulation of material wealth or institutional structure, but through the successful transfer of N — the density of meaningful action — across generations. Three falsifiable predictions are generated.
